answer_context.question: How are authentication and authorization different?

sources.supporting_passage: Authentication establishes the identity of a caller using credentials or an existing session. Authorization decides whether that identity may perform a specific action on a resource. In this course authentication is a prerequisite for authorization, and authorization is a prerequisite for document access control. A successful login alone does not grant permission to every PDF in an application.

Authorization evaluates whether a caller may perform an action on a resource. For a private PDF, compare the verified caller identity with the document owner or an explicit sharing rule. Authentication is a prerequisite for authorization. Authorization is a prerequisite for document access control. These checks belong on the server and must cover previews, retrieval, downloads, deletion, and graph queries, even if the interface hides buttons.

answer_context.question: Does HTTPS prove a website is honest or prevent phishing?

sources.supporting_passage: HTTPS carries HTTP messages over TLS. To understand HTTPS, study TLS first and HTTP before TLS. This makes HTTP a foundational prerequisite two steps before HTTPS. HTTPS protects traffic between browser and server against passive reading and modification in transit. It does not repair application authorization bugs, prevent a malicious server from storing data, or guarantee that a website is honest.

Phishing uses deceptive messages or websites to persuade a person to disclose credentials or perform an unsafe action. A message may manufacture urgency to discourage checking the sender. Verify unexpected requests through a separate trusted channel. HTTPS can encrypt a phishing website's traffic, so a secure connection is not proof that the operator is trustworthy. This lesson distinguishes transport protection from human deception.

answer_context.question: Why do ingestion retries need idempotency?

sources.supporting_passage: Idempotency means repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once. Deterministic chunk identifiers and upserts can prevent a repeated ingestion attempt from creating duplicate vectors. Transactions are a prerequisite for studying idempotency in this workflow, and idempotency is a prerequisite for safe retries. Idempotency does not mean every attempt succeeds; the operation must still report failures.

Safe retries repeat a transiently failed operation under a bounded attempt budget. Their direct prerequisite is idempotency, whose prerequisite is transactions. Use a delay or backoff when a provider is busy and stop retrying permanent input errors. If an earlier write may already have succeeded, deterministic identifiers help make the next attempt safe. Blindly repeating a non-idempotent action can duplicate data or effects.

answer_context.question: Why cannot a PostgreSQL rollback remove partial Qdrant writes?

sources.supporting_passage: A database transaction groups related changes into a unit that commits or rolls back. For a document workflow, authoritative metadata can record which processing stage completed. A SQL transaction does not automatically roll back writes made to an external vector database or object store. In this course transactions are a prerequisite for idempotency, and idempotency is a prerequisite for safe retries.

Compensating cleanup removes partial derived artifacts after a workflow fails across services. A PostgreSQL rollback cannot erase points already written to Qdrant. Delete by the exact upload identifier and preserve authoritative metadata until cleanup can be retried. Cleanup is not a distributed atomic transaction: it can also fail, so record the failure and keep operations idempotent.

answer_context.question: How are service readiness and HTTP 429 different?

sources.supporting_passage: Readiness decides whether a service can accept useful traffic. Required dependencies such as the authoritative database must work. An optional concept graph may be reported as degraded while vector-based answers continue. A healthy process does not prove that an external AI provider has quota. Readiness and rate-limit failures require different operator responses.

An HTTP 401 response means authentication is required or the supplied credentials are not accepted. An HTTP 403 response means the request is forbidden; it can occur even when identity is known. HTTP 429 indicates too many requests and can include a Retry-After header. HTTP 503 indicates that a service is temporarily unavailable. Clients should distinguish these cases rather than report every failure as an invalid password.

candidate_pages.text: A database transaction groups related changes into a unit that commits or rolls back. For a document workflow, authoritative metadata can record which processing stage completed. A SQL transaction does not automatically roll back writes made to an external vector database or object store. In this course transactions are a prerequisite for idempotency, and idempotency is a prerequisite for safe retries.

Idempotency means repeating an operation has the same intended effect as performing it once. Deterministic chunk identifiers and upserts can prevent a repeated ingestion attempt from creating duplicate vectors. Transactions are a prerequisite for studying idempotency in this workflow, and idempotency is a prerequisite for safe retries. Idempotency does not mean every attempt succeeds; the operation must still report failures.

Safe retries repeat a transiently failed operation under a bounded attempt budget. Their direct prerequisite is idempotency, whose prerequisite is transactions. Use a delay or backoff when a provider is busy and stop retrying permanent input errors. If an earlier write may already have succeeded, deterministic identifiers help make the next attempt safe. Blindly repeating a non-idempotent action can duplicate data or effects.
